n1_requests_12m.definition: Distinct 311 request ids filed in the 365 days to the run date.
n1_requests_12m.label: observed
n1_requests_12m.derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID). Counted distinct request ids; the city's CSV repeats about 7% of ids once per caller, so row counts run higher.

n1_open_backlog_2023plus.definition: Requests filed since 1 Jan 2023 whose status is neither closed nor cancelled.
n1_open_backlog_2023plus.label: observed
n1_open_backlog_2023plus.derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID). Status compared case-insensitively (the file has 'Closed' beside 'CLOSED').

n1_open_over_a_year.definition: Of the open backlog filed since 2023, those filed more than 365 days before the run date.
n1_open_over_a_year.label: observed
n1_open_over_a_year.derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID). Age measured from the filing time to the latest filing time in the file.

n1_promise_populated.definition: Share of requests carrying the city's own promised completion date (PRJCOMPLETEDATE).
n1_promise_populated.label: observed
n1_promise_populated.derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID). PRJCOMPLETEDATE is a fixed offset per request type (3 days for a light out, 90 for weeds at a vacant building).

n1_open_past_promise.definition: Open requests whose city-set promised date has passed (the Monday list), all years, sensitive codes excluded.
n1_open_past_promise.label: observed

n1_open_past_promise_12m.definition: Monday-list requests filed in the last 365 days.

n1_open_past_promise_12m.derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID). As n1_open_past_promise, restricted to the last year's filings.

n1_ledger_coverage_by_year.definition: Grass cuts ('Grass Maint' + 'Weed-Grass') per year in the forestry ledger: distinct parcel, date and service type; the raw ledger rows behind them; and the parcels covered.
n1_ledger_coverage_by_year.label: observed
n1_ledger_coverage_by_year.note: Negative result: do not use 2025 ledger figures as evidence of no cut. Use cuts_distinct_parcel_days, not ledger_rows, for any count of cuts (N8 finding 10).
n1_ledger_coverage_by_year.derivation: the Forestry Division's service ledger (forestry-service-records.csv, cuts = 'Grass Maint' and 'Weed-Grass' rows). The ledger repeats rows (most pre-2021 legacy rows appear twice), so cuts are counted as distinct parcel, date and type. 2025 is about a third of a normal year; whether cuts went unrecorded or unbilled after the 16 May tornado is not known from the file.

n1_ledger_2026.definition: Grass Maint in the forestry ledger in 2026: raw ledger rows; distinct cuts (parcel and date); the parcels they cover; and how many of those are LRA (city land bank) parcels.
n1_ledger_2026.label: observed
n1_ledger_2026.note: Say 'about 31,500 grass cuts billed on 11,971 parcels', not '37,543 cuts' (37,543 is ledger rows; N8 finding 10).
n1_ledger_2026.derivation: the Forestry Division's service ledger (forestry-service-records.csv, cuts = 'Grass Maint' and 'Weed-Grass' rows), parcel ids looked up in the LRA inventory (LRA_INVENTORY.csv). n1_mowing_gaps.label: observed
n1_mowing_gaps.note: Say 'went more than 90 days without a billed cut (counting to 30 September)' (N8 finding 15d). The city's rotation runs about eight weeks between cuts, so BUILD-SPEC's 42-day threshold flags almost every lot.
n1_mowing_gaps.derivation: the Forestry Division's service ledger (forestry-service-records.csv, cuts = 'Grass Maint' and 'Weed-Grass' rows), parcel ids looked up in the LRA inventory; a cut is a distinct parcel and date. Posting dates are batched weekly, so gaps are good to about a week.

n1_tree_cancel_wo_address.note: Say "appear in Forestry's work orders about five times as often as unrelated requests", not "were converted".

Samples cover 1,500 of 2,522 removals and 1,500 of 6,276 trims, so both shares are lower bounds.

n1_tree_blank_cancel_order_already_open.definition: Inspect City Tree requests cancelled with no words, filed more than a day after a Forestry removal order at the same normalised address had started (the order still open in the city's sample); median days the most recent such order had been open; for comparison, the count when any removal order within 30 m is allowed; and all blank-cancelled requests.
n1_tree_blank_cancel_order_already_open.label: observed
n1_tree_blank_cancel_order_already_open.note: Public text: use the same-address count (N8 conflict 3); within 30 m reaches neighbouring trees. N5 registers 288 / 575 days (n5_tree_cancel_blank_wo_predates, n5_tree_predating_wo_median_age_days) for the same rule; N1's view gives one more request. Framing (COMMON 9): residents report a tree the city already knows must come down; the request is cancelled with no words; the order stays open.
n1_tree_blank_cancel_order_already_open.derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID) matched by identical normalised address to Cityworks tree work-order samples (city map server saved searches, 1,500 rows each, staff fields removed) (removal orders, saved search 6955); Cityworks dates converted from UTC to Central. Lower bounds: the sample holds 1,500 of 2,522 open removal orders.

n6_brief_pothole_first_week_below_half.label: observed

Recent weeks still have open requests, so their shares can only fall.
